outcome: poor outcomes in fetuses and newborns
cohort: The study included 123 patients with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) and 121 healthy pregnant women as a control group.
finding: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) endanger maternal and infant health, with specific risk factors including age, BMI, parity, and history of hypertension linked to its occurrence, and resulting in higher incidences of poor maternal and infant outcomes as well as altered neonatal blood parameters.
mod_finding: The cesarean section rate was significantly higher in the HDP group compared to the control group.
